cohorts.subjects: Dry, macerated adult skeletons of the Raymond Dart Collection, Department of Anatomy (the author is at the University of Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa; the paper does not name the anatomy department's university). Groups as printed: "white" caucasoid; South African Zulu negroid; South African Sotho negroid (the paper's 1977 terms). Inclusion: adult skeletons; exclusion: 49 lumbar vertebrae missing or damaged were left out. No other criterion stated. The abstract prints 433 skeletons; Methods, Results and Conclusions print 443, which the group counts sum to. The radiological lower limits (15 and 20 mm) are this cohort's skeletal limits converted with the magnification factors of the radiograph substudy.
cohorts.n_units: 2,166 lumbar vertebrae (L1 to L5) of 443 skeletons: caucasoid 113 (78 male, 35 female), Zulu 162 (108 male, 54 female), Sotho 168 (106 male, 62 female)
cohorts.ages: 16 to 96 years at death, mean 50 (p. 173); group means 66, 49, 41 (male caucasoid, Zulu, Sotho) and 65, 47, 40 (female) in Table IV, p. 176
cohorts.sexes: 292 male, 151 female (sums of the printed group counts)

cohorts.subjects: Fifty-five dry lumbar vertebrae of eleven skeletons, suspended in sponge blocks to mimic the position of a patient's vertebrae, with radio-opaque metal markers placed in the canal at the mid-sagittal posterior limit; Fig. 1 is a lateral radiograph of a macerated spine with the markers. Whether the eleven skeletons are among the 443 is not stated. Also holds the general statement that the lateral beam crosses up to 8 cm of bone.

techniques.how: Each vertebra measured in transverse and antero-posterior diameters of the canal and the body, as described by Jones and Thomson (1968). Canal A.P. (mid-sagittal): one reading where it is least, near the canal's upper limit, opposite a slight forward bulge of the posterior wall in the midline. Canal transverse: the greatest interpedicular distance. Body A.P.: mid-sagittal at mid-height, to exclude border osteophytes. Body transverse: the greatest mid-waist distance. Tables II and III give per-group means over L1 to L5, a range of normal and the vertebrae below its lower limit; how the range was set is not stated. The 55 substudy vertebrae were measured this way before radiography.
techniques.magnification: none: true size on dry bone

techniques.instrument: plain lateral radiograph, Roentgen tube 110 cm from the plate; metal markers at the mid-sagittal posterior canal limit
techniques.how: The caliper measurements were repeated on the films. Posterior canal limit, L1 to L4: opposite the cephalad half of the body, on the line joining the apex of the superior facet and the inverted apex of the inferior facet; at L5 just anterior to the radiolucent lake of the spinous process (Fig. 2). Anterior limit: the posterior body margin in the midline, well demarcated.
techniques.magnification: factor 1.23 calculated for the lateral view; the 13 mm skeletal mid-sagittal limit gives a radiological limit of 15 mm

techniques.instrument: plain antero-posterior radiograph, Roentgen tube 110 cm from the plate
techniques.how: Interpedicular distance between the pedicle margins, which are well demarcated on the film; caliper values repeated on the films.
techniques.magnification: factor 1.14 calculated for the AP view; the 18 mm skeletal interpedicular limit gives a radiological limit of 20 mm

techniques.instrument: direct inspection of the dry skeletal material; facet joints judged in the articulated skeleton
techniques.how: Presence or absence of osteophytosis, graded mild, moderate or severe by defined descriptions, with its site (bodies, facets or both); facet shape; trefoil canal; lumbarisation of S1, persistent S1-S2 apophysial joints, sixth lumbar and transitional vertebrae, sacralisation of L5, sacro-transverse joints, sacro-iliac fusion, spondylolysis, spina bifida and wedge compression, counted per skeleton.
techniques.observers: not stated; the grading is called subjective

techniques.instrument: computed from the four caliper diameters
techniques.how: Product of the two canal diameters as a ratio of the product of the two body diameters; Jones and Thomson's lower limit of normal, 1:4.5, applied to this sample.

techniques.instrument: myelography, as quoted from Epstein, Epstein and Lavine (1962)

within_paper: The six groups are disjoint subsets of the same 443 skeletons (p. 173). The four diameters of Table I were taken on the same 2,166 vertebrae, so each vertebra is measured four ways; Tables II and III summarise the two canal rows over the same vertebrae, and the 2 skeletons stenotic in both diameters are counted in both tables (p. 174; Inference from 9 + 21 = 28 + 2, the paper does not say so). Table IV and the variant and anomaly counts are observations on the same skeletons (p. 174-177). The 55 vertebrae of 11 skeletons were measured with the caliper and again on AP and lateral radiographs, the same vertebrae by two methods (p. 174); whether those 11 skeletons are among the 443 is not stated. Inference: Figs. 3, 4 and 5 (p. 177, PDF 5) show bones carrying the same handwritten label 3292, so they are probably one skeleton photographed three times; Figs. 6 and 7 (p. 178, PDF 6) carry other labels.
